current_leader.name: Merchant settlement acceleration decision engine
current_leader.state_transition: processor balance becomes instant-eligible -> free standard settlement ETA and paid instant/same-day alternatives are known -> external bank/AP obligations determine the minimum cash needed before free settlement -> choose zero, same-day, or instant and only the minimum amount -> avoid unnecessary acceleration fees without causing a liquidity shortfall
current_leader.why_survived: Paid settlement acceleration remains a real recurring decision with explicit fee schedules and machine-readable payout state. Stripe charges 1%-1.5% for Instant Payouts while non-accelerated funds continue on the free default schedule. Razorpay publishes 0.20%-0.30% instant and 0.15%-0.20% same-day settlement and explicitly allows merchants to settle the needed amount. Broad treasury and D2C finance systems forecast cash and gateway settlements, but no exact product was found this run that combines processor balances, live external liquidity, AP due dates and settlement-fee tiers to calculate the minimum paid acceleration amount and cheapest speed tier.
current_leader.closest_threat: Adjacent products are closer than previously scored. FlowOne forecasts cash and optimizes payment timing; SeerFlow combines Razorpay settlements with forward cash-flow forecasting; TreasuryPath continuously optimizes cash positions. Razorpay itself already lets merchants select the needed settlement amount. The remaining whitespace is fee-aware calculation of zero/same-day/instant using external obligations and bank liquidity.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read-only v1: ingest processor available/instant-eligible balance, free settlement ETA and acceleration fee tiers; ingest authorized bank balance and obligations due before each ETA; output the minimum amount and cheapest speed tier required. Do not initiate money movement.
current_leader.monetization: Small per-decision or monthly fee, or capped share of verified acceleration fees avoided relative to a documented competent-treasury baseline.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: The avoidable fee pool remains unquantified and incumbent absorption risk increased. Merchants may already accelerate only what they genuinely need, in which case incremental savings after competent manual treasury practice are too small.
current_leader.next_research_test: Find merchant-level evidence on frequency and size of paid accelerated settlements, simulate optimal decisions using actual due-date obligations, and measure avoidable fees after a competent manual baseline. Search exact products integrating Stripe/Razorpay/Cashfree balances, live bank balances, AP due dates and settlement fee tiers. Kill if incremental avoidable fees are immaterial or exact automation already exists.

recent_cross_family_findings: Paid settlement acceleration remains a real speed-versus-fee decision, but Razorpay itself already supports choosing the needed settlement amount, so amount selection alone is not whitespace.

SeerFlow connects Shopify and Razorpay and forecasts day-by-day D2C cash positions from settlements and obligations, but currently states that it does not read a live bank-account balance; this narrows rather than eliminates the settlement-optimizer wedge.
FlowOne and TreasuryPath show that cash forecasting and autonomous cash optimization are becoming standard treasury capabilities, increasing first-party/adjacent absorption risk for the leader.

Generic B2B payment-rail speed optimization is rejected: PayLoom explicitly chooses ACH standard, same-day ACH, RTP/FedNow, wire and other rails by due-date urgency, discounts and cost; Niural similarly picks the cheapest/fastest path.
The leader must be judged against competent manual treasury behavior, not a naive baseline that accelerates the entire processor balance.
known_rejected_or_demoted_summary: Full historical rejection list is preserved in prior anchor blobs and immutable run files. Do not revive prior rejected families without materially new mechanism/evidence.
